global_organization_chain: Name the physical design object and optimization intent in the title.
Translate judged performance into two operational objectives: vertical air and rotation.
Decompose current half-pipe engineering into components, dimensions, and historical baselines.
State the geometric and mechanical abstraction before any derivation.
Build the vertical-air branch by escalating from conservative invariance to a travel-time objective, then to frictional path dynamics and candidate-family simulations.
Repeat candidate comparisons under width, length, and friction controls, then surface physical and numerical boundaries.
Build the rotation branch from a fixed-period ballistic baseline and extend it qualitatively through pumping and deeper landing.
Close by exposing the conflict between the two objectives and converting it into practical design criteria rather than claiming one universal shape.

main_argument_chains.claim: Frictionless vertical air is invariant to cross-section shape, so a separate spectator-oriented time objective is needed.
support_steps: Equal coping heights and fixed initial energy make exit energy path-independent.
The paper introduces coping-to-midpoint travel time without relabeling it as vertical air.
A variational derivation maps the time functional to a cycloid and pairs it with a rolling-circle construction.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the cycloid only for the idealized travel-time objective; do not treat it as the practical vertical-air optimum once friction and feasibility enter.

main_argument_chains.claim: Under the paper's friction model, candidate geometry affects exit response through width, arc length, and curvature-dependent normal loss.
support_steps: Arc-length geometry feeds a normal-force and Coulomb-loss balance.
Semicircle, cycloid, and two flat-oval instances supply common geometry outputs.
Fixed-width and fixed-length comparisons are reported separately.
Width and friction sweeps make the long flat oval the strongest tested family while exposing a degenerate boundary.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the ranking as conditional on the printed candidate set, controls, and passive-loss model, while retaining the paper's useful geometry-to-force-to-output organization.

main_argument_chains.claim: With fixed athlete rotation period, more airtime permits more rotations, and pumping is proposed as a mechanism for extending airtime.
support_steps: The no-pumping branch reduces flight to vertical projectile motion.
Airtime is divided by a fixed rotation period to define rotation count.
The pumping branch adds a horizontal takeoff component and a deeper landing narrative.
Landing stills are used to make the proposed mechanism visually legible.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the clean baseline-to-mechanism progression, but label the pumping branch qualitative until takeoff, flight, angular motion, and landing are modeled and measured.

main_argument_chains.claim: The vertical-air and rotation branches favor opposing course geometries, so practical design requires explicit tradeoff criteria.
support_steps: The vertical-air branch trends toward low, narrow, low-loss shapes.
The rotation narrative favors deeper and wider geometry for longer pumped flight.
The limitations section names load, flex, slope, drag, and construction considerations.
The conclusion returns to the two objectives and refuses a false universal optimum.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Carry the two-branch architecture into a constrained multi-objective decision rather than ending at an unweighted preference statement.
